vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.7.0

The 'here-now' skill bundle provides a legitimate utility for publishing static files and folders to the here.now hosting service. The core logic in scripts/publish.sh implements a standard three-step upload flow (initialize, upload to presigned URLs, and finalize) and includes reasonable security practices such as validating the API endpoint before sending credentials and setting restrictive permissions on the local credentials file (~/.herenow/credentials).

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (publishes files to here.now) but the package metadata, installation hints, and some instructions are inconsistent or encourage running remote installers—review before trusting with sensitive files or credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (static hosting) matches the script's behavior (builds a file manifest, requests presigned upload URLs, uploads files, finalizes). However registry metadata declared no required binaries/env, while SKILL.md and scripts require curl, file, jq and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY and ~/.herenow/credentials. The npx install string in SKILL.md references 'heredotnow/skill' (name mismatch) which is inconsistent with the skill slug and source.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run scripts that read files, compute hashes, read ~/.herenow/credentials or $HERENOW_API_KEY, create/overwrite .herenow/state.json in the working directory, and POST to here.now endpoints. All are coherent with hosting, but the script hints (and SKILL.md) recommend an agent-assisted sign-up flow (collect email + one-time code) and include instructions that could prompt the agent to ask for and handle user credentials/API keys. The script also suggests installing jq by running a remote installer (curl ... | bash) hosted on here.now—this encourages executing remote code and is a scope/behavior risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no platform install spec), which is low risk, but SKILL.md suggests installing via 'npx skills add heredotnow/skill' (package name mismatch) and the script prints a curl|bash command (https://here.now/install.sh) to install jq. Those suggestions reference external code and could lead to executing remote installers; that's higher-risk than a pure instruction-only skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script only requires an API key for persistent/owned sites and will work anonymously otherwise; it reads $HERENOW_API_KEY and ~/.herenow/credentials and writes ~/.herenow/credentials if told to save a key. That is proportionate to the stated purpose. The registry metadata claiming 'no required env vars' is inconsistent with the SKILL.md/script.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and only writes its own local state (.herenow/state.json) and optionally ~/.herenow/credentials. It can be invoked autonomously (default) which is expected for skills; this combined with the ability to ask users for an email/code increases agent capability but is not inherently a privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement a legitimate static-hosting flow, but take these precautions before installing or using it:

- Verify the author and endpoints: the script talks to https://here.now; confirm you trust that domain. The SKILL.md's npx recommendation uses 'heredotnow/skill' which doesn't match the slug—double-check the official package source before running npx.
- Avoid running remote installers: the script's error message suggests running 'curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash' to install jq. Do NOT run curl|bash from an unfamiliar domain; prefer installing jq from your system package manager or a trusted project release.
- Be careful with credentials and sensitive files: anonymous publishes upload your files to the service (they expire after 24h). Do not publish secrets or private data. If you provide an API key for permanent sites, the script will read/write ~/.herenow/credentials—store and manage that file securely.
- Review the script yourself: the skill includes scripts/publish.sh — inspect the full file (and any bundled binaries) before running. Ensure there is no unexpected network endpoint, telemetry, or code execution beyond uploading site content.
- If you only need temporary sharing, use anonymous mode and avoid saving an API key. If you plan to save an API key, create it via the official dashboard or confirm the agent-mediated flow's security and that the returned apiKey is stored only in ~/.herenow/credentials with proper permissions.

If you want a firmer assessment, provide the remaining truncated portion of scripts/publish.sh (the save-state code) and confirm where you would get the 'npx' package from. That would increase confidence in the evaluation.
